shared_context.content: For noncollinear points A,B,C in the Euclidean plane R^2, circ(A,B,C) denotes the circumcenter of triangle ABC, i.e. the unique point equidistant from A,B,C, equivalently the unique intersection point of the perpendicular bisectors of AB and AC.
shared_context.label: Circumcenter definition

shared_context.content: If f : R^2 -> {red,green} is a 2-coloring, define R_f = {P in R^2 | f(P)=red} and G_f = {P in R^2 | f(P)=green}.
shared_context.label: Color classes

strategy_summary: Reformulate the hypothesis as a closure property for each color class, then combine two external geometric-combinatorial facts: (i) any 2-coloring of the Euclidean plane contains a monochromatic equilateral triangle, and (ii) any nonempty subset of the plane that is closed under taking circumcenters of noncollinear triples is either contained in a line or equals the whole plane. The monochromatic equilateral triangle rules out the 'contained in a line' case, forcing one color class to be all of R^2.
